  : Tests with four or more boxes at framing zero. "Cases" is the total number of $\rho$ tested; "terms" is the sum over $\rho$ of the numbers of terms of the spin form at the largest number of boxes. There are no negative terms in the spin form or in the genus form. {#tbl-higher}

The ranges were chosen as follows. At four boxes the non-hook color $\ydBB$ and the Adams images $(a,q,t)\mapsto(a^2,q^2,t^2)$ of $\ydB$ and $\ydAA$ enter $\widehat{f}_\rho$ for the first time. At six boxes the Adams operations with $d=2,3,6$ have appeared for all colors with at most three boxes. From seven boxes on no new type of term appears and only the size grows. The knots were chosen by the number of strands, i.e. the width in the $a$-degree: $T_{2,2k+1}$ are thin, $T_{3,n}$ are thick of width $2$, and $T_{4,5}$ has width $3$. The overall sign was $-1$ for $|\rho|\equiv2\pmod4$ and $+1$ otherwise, uniformly for all $\rho$ with the same number of boxes. For odd $|\rho|$ the half-integer shift of the $a$-degree is the periodic continuation of the convention of KN for $|\rho|=1,3$; it shifts $\beta$ uniformly and does not affect positivity. The coefficients of the genus form grow rapidly with the number of boxes: up to about $10^{30}$ for $T_{2,3}$ with nine boxes, and already about $10^{21}$ for $T_{4,5}$ with three boxes.

## A weak test for the figure-eight knot with four boxes {#sec-fig8-four}

For $\mathbf{4_1}$ with four boxes the rectangular inputs $\ydD$, $\ydBB$, $\ydAAAA$ come from the refined formulas of KNTZ [@Kameyama19]; they agree in all coefficients with the values of KN for $\ydA$ to $\ydAAA$ and with the GNSSS formulas for the symmetric colors $[r]$, $r\le4$. For $\ydBA$ we use the KN candidate. The refined value for $\ydCA$, and for its transpose $\ydBAA$, is not in the literature. We therefore treat the coefficients of $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydCA}$ as unknowns subject to the following linear conditions:

- at $t=q$ it equals the differential expansion of Morozov [@Morozov16] for $\ydCA$ (for $\mathbf{4_1}$, a sum of $Z$-factors);

- transposition, $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydBAA}(a,q,t)=\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydCA}(a,t^{-1},q^{-1})$, and amphichirality;

- exponential growth: it equals $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydAA}\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydA}^2$ at $q=1$ and $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydC}\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydA}$ at $t=1$;

- at $a=t^2$ it equals $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydB}\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydAA}$ (reduction to $U(2)$; a hypothesis);

- all $\widehat{f}_\rho$ with $|\rho|=4$ are Laurent polynomials, the genus expansion closes, and they are positive.

Since $\widehat{f}_\rho$ is linear in $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydCA}$, with a denominator depending only on $q,t$, these are conditions of a linear program.

::: {#exr-fig8-four}
With the unknowns restricted to $2367$ monomials determined from the values at the specializations, the following hold. With overall sign $-1$ the problem is infeasible, already with positivity of the spin form alone. With overall sign $+1$ there exists a rational solution for which both forms are non-negative. The existence of an integral solution is undecided (Appendix [A](#sec-app-computation)).
:::

This is not a test of the conjecture; it only shows that, over the rationals, an $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydCA}$ compatible with the conjecture exists at four boxes. The conclusion depends on the KN candidate for $\ydBA$, on the $U(2)$ hypothesis, and on the range of unknowns. The formulation was checked on $T_{2,3}$, for which $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydCA}$ is known from the elliptic Hall algebra: the true value satisfies all conditions and lies in the range of unknowns, and the $\widehat{f}_\rho$ assembled from it agree with the direct computation.

## The structure of the KN candidate for $\ydBA$ {#sec-fig8-21}

KN state that their candidate for $\mathbf{4_1}$ colored by $\ydBA$ was found by imposing mirror symmetry, exponential growth and amphichirality [@Kameyama17]. It can be written in terms of the $Z$-factor expansion of Anokhina et al. [@Anokhina12]. Let $(A,Q,T)=(a,q,t)^{1/2}$, $\{z\}=z-z^{-1}$ and $\mathfrak{Z}_{I|J}^{(s|\sigma)}=\{AQ^{I+s}T^{-\sigma}\}\{AQ^sT^{-J-\sigma}\}$, with $\mathfrak{Z}_{I|J}=\mathfrak{Z}_{I|J}^{(0|0)}$.

::: {#exr-fig8-21}
The KN candidate equals $$\begin{multline*}
1+\bigl(\mathfrak{Z}^{(-1|-1)}_{3|3}+\mathfrak{Z}^{(1|0)}_{1|1}+\mathfrak{Z}^{(0|1)}_{1|1}\bigr)
+\bigl(\mathfrak{Z}^{(0|-1)}_{3|3}\mathfrak{Z}^{(1|0)}_{1|1}+\mathfrak{Z}^{(-1|0)}_{3|3}\mathfrak{Z}^{(0|1)}_{1|1}+\alpha\,\mathfrak{Z}^{(1|0)}_{1|1}\mathfrak{Z}^{(0|1)}_{1|1}\bigr)\\
+\mathfrak{Z}_{3|3}\mathfrak{Z}^{(1|0)}_{1|1}\mathfrak{Z}^{(0|1)}_{1|1}
\end{multline*}$$ with $\alpha=1-\{Q\}\{T\}$. Anokhina et al. take the same expression with $\alpha=1-(Q-T^{-1})(T-Q^{-1})$ and obtain a superpolynomial with all coefficients positive. In bold variables the KN candidate has $69$ terms of which $10$ are negative, and its value at $\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{q}=\mathbf{t}=1$ is $125=5^3$, the cube of the value for $\ydA$; for the expression of Anokhina et al. the value is $189$.
:::

At $t=q$ both choices of $\alpha$ reduce to $1-(Q-Q^{-1})^2$. Thus the KN candidate corresponds to imposing exponential growth instead of positivity of the superpolynomial.

We also examined the condition of Heegaard--Floer type proposed by Anokhina et al. for hook colors $\lambda=[r,1^{s-1}]$: $$
\mathrm{rCS}_\lambda\bigl(A=T/Q\,\big|\,Q,T\bigr)=\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydA}\bigl(A=T/Q\,\big|\,Q^rT^{s-1},\,T^sQ^{r-1}\bigr).
$$ {#eq-HF}

::: {#exr-HF}
([-@eq-HF]) holds for $\mathbf{4_1}$ with $\ydBA$, both for the KN candidate and for the expression of Anokhina et al. For the elliptic Hall algebra values of $T_{2,3}$, $T_{2,5}$, $T_{3,4}$ with $\ydBA$ and $\ydCA$ it holds up to the monomial $(T/Q)^{\delta(|\lambda|-1)}$.
:::

Condition ([-@eq-HF]) is a linear condition that was not included in the linear program above.

Finally, we tried to extend the method of KN to $\ydCA$ by decomposing the value of Morozov at $t=q$ into the form of Anokhina et al.: one product of shifted $Z$-factors for each subset of boxes, with corrections of the coefficients only for disconnected subsets. For $\ydBA$ this search reproduces the expansion of Anokhina et al. as the unique solution. For $\ydCA$ there is no decomposition of this form with shifts $|k|\le2$, and none in which the shifts are sums of contributions of pairs of boxes. The color $\ydCA$ seems to require structure beyond products over subsets.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

We extended the refined large $N$ duality of KN to framed knots and tested the positivity of the spin form and the genus form of the refined LMOV invariants. With defined inputs (torus knots and algebraic iterated torus knots) no negative term was found in any case examined, up to three boxes for cables, up to between five and nine boxes for torus knots (Table [-@tbl-higher]), and over ranges of framings. For the cables this holds under the normalization hypothesis (Hypothesis [-@exm-N2]). With homological or conjectural inputs, positivity is a theorem for $\ydA$ and is proved for families of twist and double twist knots for two boxes.

For individual knots the exponential-polynomial structure in $x$ and the Newton criterion reduce positivity for all $x$ to finitely many checks (Theorem [-@thm-two-all-x]). This is a knot-by-knot argument and not a theorem for general knots. It is open whether the positivity of the Newton coefficients can be derived from properties of the input such as non-negativity and $\sigma$-invariance of homology. Certificates are also missing for twist knots with $p$ and $x$ of opposite signs and for three boxes at all $x$. We did not compare the framed unknot with the refined open BPS invariants of toric branes of Cheng and Sułkowski [@Cheng21]. On the physical side, we showed that the Mariño--Vafa sign is necessary for the Laurent property (Proposition [-@prp-sign]), but we did not derive the refined shift of the flat coordinate, $V\mapsto-(q/t)^{1/2}V$, from geometry. That $U(1)_R$ acts trivially on the string side independently of the framing also remains an assumption.

Three boxes for hyperbolic knots require a definition of the refined invariant for $\ydBA$. We see three candidates: a construction through refined Racah matrices (a refinement of the arborescent calculus [@Mironov16]); an extension of the DAHA or elliptic Hall algebra definition to hyperbolic knots (the genus-two DAHA is so far limited to $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ [@Arthamonov15]); and a computation of HOMFLY-PT homology colored by $\ydBA$ together with a rule converting it to $\overline{\mathrm{rCS}}$. All are beyond the scope of this paper. For $\mathbf{4_1}$ with four boxes the color $\ydCA$ poses the same problem (§[-@sec-fig8-four]). The KN candidate for $\ydBA$ fits the $Z$-factor expansion of Anokhina et al. (Computational Result [-@exr-fig8-21]), but no expansion of the same form was found for $\ydCA$. The condition ([-@eq-HF]) of Heegaard--Floer type holds for the elliptic Hall algebra values and can serve as a new constraint on $\ydCA$.

The closed formula for the monomial normalization (Computational Result [-@exr-M]) was derived under the refined satellite formula (Hypothesis [-@exm-sat]). Since the DAHA and the elliptic Hall algebra do not determine the monomial, this hypothesis remains a physical assumption. For torus knots, the form of the corollary of Mellit in the standard normalization was checked by computation (Computational Result [-@exr-mellit]); an explicit identification of the operators $d_\pm$ with $Q_{m,n}$ is left open. It does not affect the positivity results.

Finally, the tests for torus knots beyond three boxes are finite computations (Table [-@tbl-higher]). The coefficients of the genus form grow rapidly with the number of boxes, yet no negative term appears. A proof of positivity for all numbers of boxes from the structure of the elliptic Hall algebra is open, as are the remaining opposite-sign region for double twist knots (§[-@sec-two]) and a structural reason for the unimodality of the two-box invariants.

# Appendix A: Details of the computation {#sec-app-computation .appendix .unnumbered}

The invariants $\overline{\mathrm{rCS}}_\lambda$ and $\widehat{f}_\rho$ are evaluated modulo a $31$-bit prime $p$ on a grid and interpolated in each of the variables $(A,Q,T)=(a,q,t)^{1/2}$. When coefficients exceed $p/2$, two or three primes are used and the result is reconstructed by the Chinese remainder theorem (Garner's algorithm). The polynomials obtained are checked at points not used in the interpolation. Evaluation points are stored in blocks so that a computation can be resumed.

For the genus expansion we proceed as in Lemma [-@lem-G]: with $v=\mathbf{q}^2\mathbf{t}$, $w=v+v^{-1}$ and $w_0=\mathbf{t}+\mathbf{t}^{-1}$ we have $G=w-w_0$. Each coefficient of a power of $\mathbf{a}$ is rewritten as a polynomial in $w$ and expanded in powers of $G$ by Horner's scheme.

For $|\rho|\ge4$, $\widehat{f}_\rho$ is computed directly at each evaluation point (§[-@sec-higher]). The variable $A$ is also evaluated numerically and interpolated as a polynomial in $a=A^2$, with a check at one point outside the range. For torus knots the parities of the exponents of $Q$ and $T$ are uniform, so we interpolate in $q=Q^2$, $t=T^2$, which reduces the number of evaluation points by a factor of four. In the elliptic Hall algebra computation, the action of the operators corresponding to the power sums and its evaluation are shared across the colors $\lambda$. With eight parallel processes, the running times for the largest number of boxes of each knot in Table [-@tbl-higher] were $428$ s for $T_{2,3}$, $299$ s for $T_{2,5}$, $1260$ s for $T_{2,7}$, $2036$ s for $T_{2,9}$, $280$ s for $T_{3,4}$, $322$ s for $T_{3,5}$, $64$ s for $T_{3,7}$ and $474$ s for $T_{4,5}$. In the weak test of §[-@sec-fig8-four], the mixed integer program with overall sign $+1$ was stopped after $50$ minutes without an integral solution, which leaves its existence undecided.

The computations were done on an Apple M3 Pro with $36$ GB of memory and a Mac mini M1 with $8$ GB. The heaviest case is $K10$: $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydC}$ took about four hours ($14440$ s) with two primes and $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydBA}$ about two hours ($7387$ s). The three-box $\widehat{f}_\rho$ required three primes, $4050$ s and at most $17.6$ GB of memory. For $K7$ and $K8$ all colors with $|\rho|\le3$ took $12275$ s and $22853$ s, with less than $2$ GB of memory.

Each stage of the implementation was tested on small inputs: the reproduction of the values of KN, of the explicit examples of Cherednik and Danilenko and of HOMFLY-PT polynomials computed from braids, the interpolation and the Chinese remainder theorem, and the agreement of two independent implementations of the genus expansion.

# Appendix B: Derivation of the normalization {#sec-app-normalization .appendix .unnumbered}

We give the details of the proof of Proposition [-@prp-M], first for the cabling step and then for torus knots. The framing operator $\tau:P_\mu\mapsto T_\mu P_\mu$ satisfies $\tau^jP_\lambda[p_k\mapsto P_{k(m,n)}]\cdot1=P_\lambda[p_k\mapsto P_{k(m,n+jm)}]\cdot1$ (Computational Result [-@exr-tau]). The cable construction is linear in the companion. Applying (N2$'$) to the companion shifts the slope of the pattern from $(m,-s')$ to $(m,-n)$, i.e. to the Seifert framing. Together with Hypothesis [-@exm-sat] this gives $M_{C_{m,n}K}=M_K^{\,m}M_{T_{m,n}}$ and $F=mn$.

For torus knots the four facts used in the proof are the following. (I) The coefficient of $a^0$ in the unnormalized reduced value of Gorsky and Neguţ is $(-t/q)^{m-1}C_{m,n}(1/q,t)$, where $C_{m,n}$ is the rational $q,t$-Catalan number. This was conjectured by Gorsky and Neguţ and follows from the theorem of Mellit [@Mellit16] through the operators $Q_{m,n}$ of Bergeron, Garsia, Leven and Xin. (II) The lowest $a$-degree $\delta$ follows from the theorem of Franks and Williams on positive braids [@Franks87]. (III) The sign and the power of $q$ at $t=q$ follow from the $q,t$-symmetry of $C_{m,n}$. (IV) The exponent of $(q/t)$ follows from the Dyck-path form of Mellit [@Mellit17] and Computational Result [-@exr-mellit]. Together these give $M_{T_{m,n}}=(-q/t)^{m-1}\bigl(a(q/t)^{1/2}\bigr)^{\delta}$.

The formula of Computational Result [-@exr-mellit] used in (IV) differs in form from the corollary as stated by Mellit. Mellit [@Mellit17 Cor. 3.4] writes $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}=(-1)^n(a(qt)^{-1/2})^\delta\frac{1}{1-t}\frac{P_{m,n}(1)[a-1]}{a-1}$ with $P_{m,n}$ "the corresponding generator of the elliptic Hall algebra". By Thm. 3.3 of the same paper this holds if $P_{m,n}(1)$ is read as $-d_-B_{c_{m,n}}d_+(1)$ in terms of the operators $d_\pm$ of Carlsson and Mellit. If instead it is read as the element in the standard normalization ($Q_{m,n}$ of [@Bergeron14] or $\widetilde P$ of [@Gorsky13b]), the formula with the substitution $[a-1]$ does not hold; in a comparison over four choices of the element ($Q_{m,n}\cdot1$ and $\widetilde P\cdot1$, each with both orders of the indices), eight choices of the variables ($q$ and $t$ exchanged or inverted) and the five substitutions $[a-1]$, $[a/q-1]$, $[aq-1]$, $[a/t-1]$, $[at-1]$, for $(m,n)=(2,3),(3,2),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3)$, only the form of Computational Result [-@exr-mellit] agrees with the Dyck-path form up to a monomial. Since (IV) only fixes the exponent of $(q/t)$ in $M_\square$, this point does not affect any positivity result (Lemma [-@lem-adams]).

# Appendix C: Non-algebraic cables {#sec-app-nonalg .appendix .unnumbered}

The non-algebraic cables that we computed are the $(2,1)$-, $(2,3)$-, $(2,5)$-, $(2,7)$- and $(2,-1)$-cables of $T_{2,3}$, named $K2$, $K4$, $K5a$, $K5b$, $K5c$ in this order, and the $(2,1)$-cable $K6b$ of $T_{2,5}$. These knots have $n_2<m_1n_1m_2$. For the five cables other than $K5b$ the DAHA value for $\ydA$ does not satisfy the necessary conditions coming from spectral sequences and is therefore not the Poincaré polynomial of HOMFLY-PT homology, so the premise of the KN positivity is not satisfied. Table [-@tbl-nonalg] shows the outcome of the tests.

  $K4$    non-alg.     18/42; 20/43    286/1109; 195/952    330/1255; 224/1090   2561/8614; 1749/7420     2850/9646; 1989/8325    3025/10121; 2128/8795

The failures are of three types. (I) For the $(2,3)$- and $(2,5)$-cables of $T_{2,3}$ ($K4$, $K5a$), positivity with a refinement of uniform parity is impossible already at the level of the uncolored HOMFLY-PT polynomial. (II) For the $(2,1)$-cables ($K2$, $K6b$) and the $(2,-1)$-cable ($K5c$) the HOMFLY-PT polynomial is compatible with positivity, but the DAHA value $\mathrm{rCS}_{\ydA}$ itself has negative coefficients. (III) For the $(2,7)$-cable of $T_{2,3}$ ($K5b$) the failure in the colored case depends on the framing: among even framings $|x|\le24$, both forms are positive for two boxes when $x\le-12$ and for three boxes when $x\le-14$. For the cable $K5c$ with $\rho=\ydA$ the genus form is non-negative while the spin form has $5$ negative terms among $57$, and the same happens for $\ydB$, $\ydAA$ and $\ydAAA$ (Table [-@tbl-nonalg]); this shows that the converse of Lemma [-@lem-G] fails.

# Appendix D: Data and code {#sec-app-data .appendix .unnumbered}

The code and tests used for the computation are available at <https://github.com/kameyama/refined_lmov>. The repository also contains the certificates used in the computer-assisted proofs and the computed values of $\overline{\mathrm{rCS}}_\lambda$, $\widehat{f}_\rho$, the spin form and the genus form, except those for four or more boxes, which are omitted because of their size and can be recomputed with the code.
